result.basis: a `cost_centre` bucket is one cost centre under one cost category (`category`; a centre named under two categories has two buckets) and adds the cost-centre allocations of each counted entry, each on the side its own amount's sign gives; `members` lists the ledgers whose allocations fall in it, largest movement first and at most 10; each category allocates the whole entry, so the categories overlap and their buckets are not added across categories: `category_totals` gives each category's figure, `totals` counts each allocated entry once, and `entries_unallocated` holds the counted entries with no allocation (with `totals`, every counted entry); an empty summary says that nothing in the window was allocated, not that the company's Cost Centres setting is off (allocations were read on a book with the setting at No); an entry whose allocations could not be read (`summary_cost_centre_unreadable`) or whose category does not add up to the entry (`summary_cost_centre_allocation_mismatch`) refuses the summary; every voucher the window, selectors and search selected that is not cancelled, optional or without accounting entries, as ledger_movement counts (a narrowed window is not a ledger's whole movement); post-dated vouchers are summed too: post_dated_included counts those Tally flagged Yes and post_dated_flag_absent those with no flag at all (Tally asserts the flag on every voucher the current read asks for, so that is expected to be 0; only when it is not is a zero in the first no proof that none are post-dated); a voucher type that does not post (a memorandum, a reversing journal, a sales or purchase order, a delivery or receipt note), if the book uses it and Tally exports it with ledger entries, is not told apart and is summed (none of the vouchers in the one window this was checked on were of those types; the book's voucher-type masters were not read)
